cases.why: Only the DERIVED age crosses this boundary. The DOB is never echoed.
AN INELIGIBLE APPLICANT IS A SUCCESSFUL 200. A client that treats non-2xx as 'ineligible' reads every ineligible candidate as a transport failure and vice versa.
The age gate is DOB-free by construction (ADR-006). A date of birth in this response would be a PII leak from an encrypted-at-rest column.
It does not ACCEPT one either. A UI that asks a citizen for a birth date to compute eligibility is duplicating a decision the platform makes from NIDA data, against worse input.
eligible is education.meetsRequirement, renamed on the wire.
The school and the raw index are request-only. Only the derived verdict returns.
Second member: WRONG ROAD, not a candidate failure. Use degree-check. These two must not share an error surface.

value.detail: This category requires HEC degree verification, not NESA.

cases.why: HEC_NOT_APPLICABLE belongs to the degree route's union, not this one. The two 409 unions are genuinely different sets.
The widest of the three, carrying the specialist age exception.
The degree is real and belongs to somebody else. AN ALLEGATION OF IMPERSONATION — it must not share copy with 'record not found'.
The other member of the same status. Radically different meaning.
The identity predates the G2G subject hash — remedy is to re-verify identity, which no other outcome in the platform asks for.

value.detail: Identity predates the G2G subject hash; re-verify identity.

cases.why: The G2G subject hash is an internal cross-service key, exactly like nationalIdHash. It never crosses this edge.
The G2G registry is down. Retry advice differs from our own store being down, so they are modelled apart.
Our own identity store is down.
The controller writes a caller-facing hint on this 503 and expose = status < 500 discards it. Eight such strings exist platform-wide and nobody receives any of them.

value.detail: The identity store is temporarily unavailable.

cases.why: FOUR fields, including applicationId — unlike age-check, which takes two.
The controller's NESA_INDEX_PATTERN is enforced server-side, so it is enforced here too. Backend-enforced input constraints ARE emitted; response formats are not.
